title: Capacity Shortcuts & Modern Hardware
summary: Do fast mental math only when numbers decide between one node and a distributed cluster.
body:
Perform back-of-the-envelope calculations when a number changes an architectural choice—such as whether an index fits in RAM or whether fan-out exceeds network egress—rather than reciting rote arithmetic upfront.

## Daily volume to QPS shortcuts
Use `100,000 seconds/day` (actual `86,400`) so division is instant:
- `100,000 events/day` ≈ `1 req/s`.
- `10 million events/day` ≈ `100 req/s`.
- `100 million events/day` ≈ `1,000 to 1,200 req/s` (multiply by `2x` to `10x` for peak).
- `1 billion events/day` ≈ `12,000 req/s` average.

## Modern single-server baselines
Cloud instances are far larger than 2015 textbook numbers:
- Memory: `128 GB` to `512 GB` RAM on a commodity node (`250M` geospatial points at `64 bytes` each is `16 GB`—fits in one node's RAM and replicates easily).
- Storage: local NVMe SSDs sustain `3+ GB/s` sequential throughput and hundreds of thousands of random IOPS.
- Relational DB primary: `5,000 to 15,000` simple transactional writes/s and `30,000+` indexed point reads/s.
- In-memory key-value shard: `80,000 to 150,000` single-threaded ops/s with sub-millisecond latency.
- Stateful gateway node: `50,000 to 100,000` concurrent idle WebSocket/SSE connections.

## Decisions driven by math
- Dataset under `50 GB` with heavy reads: replicate in memory instead of sharding prematurely.
- Writes above `20,000/s` or storage above a few terabytes with high growth: partition horizontally by a high-cardinality key.
- Media egress (`1M` concurrent HD streams at `5 Mbps` = `5 Tbps`): serve bytes from a CDN and pre-signed object storage, never through app servers.
